key_insight: Even when raw sensor data stays on-device, the sequence of policy gradients in embodied reinforcement learning can leak private trajectories. TRACE shows that temporal information makes gradient inversion more powerful than single-step attacks.
problem_solved: The paper addresses privacy leakage in distributed embodied RL, where servers receive per-step policy gradients and may be able to reconstruct an agent's private observation-action trajectory.
method: Introduces TRACE (Temporal Reconstruction Attack on Consecutive Encodings), an amortized temporal gradient-inversion attack.
Uses autoregressive reconstruction to recover a sequence of private observations and actions from per-step policy-gradient signals.
Exploits temporal dependencies across consecutive steps to improve reconstruction beyond frame-by-frame inversion.
impact: This work shows that gradient sharing in embodied RL may expose far more than expected, especially over time. Practitioners designing distributed RL systems should consider temporal privacy risks and stronger defenses, not just single-step gradient leakage.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: on-device agent -> per-step gradients -> server-side TRACE reconstruction
Timeline visualization showing consecutive observations/actions being recovered autoregressively
Before/after comparison of true trajectory vs reconstructed trajectory
Icon set for privacy, gradients, sequence modeling, and RL agent-environment interaction
paper_title: Temporal Gradient Inversion for Private Trajectory Reconstruction in Embodied Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Sudip Bhujel, Shanghao Shi, Ruiquan Huang, Ning Zhang, Yang Xiao
